description: coaxial-fuse's rod moved four tolerances (4e-7) off the tube's axis along +x, fused: the rod's wall 4e-7 into the tube's on that side, and on the other a crescent between them up to 4e-7 wide, four tolerances, open through the whole height — a hole, genus 1, as it is with the rod moved the other way (coaxial-fuse-four-off-back). For a unit bore and rod of height 2 at offset d the crescent's area is 2·asin(d/2) + (d/2)√(4 − d²) = 2d − d³/12 + O(d⁵), its two walls together 2π·2 long, so the volume is 8π − 4d + d³/6 and the area 20π − 4d + d³/6; the centroid is at x = d/8, and to first order in d the inertia about it is 32π/3 − 8d/3, 32π/3 − 4d and 16π − 4d (products zero by symmetry), within 1e-13 of exact. Arris's STEP, read by Open CASCADE, gives every one of them to 1e-11, and the same as the mirror image does (coaxial-fuse-four-off-back, whose oracle agrees). Open CASCADE's own fuse on this side closes the crescent and measures the coaxial union, 8π and 16π — a mirror image measured differently, so the oracle is the one that is wrong (ADR-0015) (plans/c3-tolerance-apart step 9, the band's ends).

analytic.counts_differ: Open CASCADE closes the crescent on this side, merging the bore's wall and the rod's where they lie within 4e-7 of each other (10/13/7/9, genus 0), though it keeps it open with the rod moved the other way; Arris keeps it open both ways, four tolerances wide
analytic.measure_differs: Open CASCADE's fuse closes the 4e-7 crescent on this side and measures the coaxial union (volume 8π, area 16π), where it measures the mirror image with the crescent open; the closed forms of the description hold, and Arris's STEP meets them
